entities.summary: Archibald MacLeish was an American poet and writer, who was associated with the modernist school of poetry. MacLeish studied English at Yale University and law at Harvard University. He enlisted in and saw action during the First World War and lived in Paris in the 1920s. On returning to the United States, he contributed to Henry Luce's magazine Fortune from 1929 to 1938. For five years, MacLeish was the ninth Librarian of Congress, a post he accepted at the urging of President Franklin D. Roosevelt. Archibald MacLeish was a writers & intellectuals from Glencoe (1892-05-07, Glencoe–1982-04-20). A moderately significant entity in the historical record. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As the ninth Librarian of Congress from 1938 to 1950, MacLeish played a crucial role in shaping the cultural and intellectual landscape of post-war America. His tenure saw significant investments in literary programs and collections, contributing to the preservation of American literature for future generations.
